title: Tunes from a studio session credited to someone else; ASCAP
summary: Claire Stewart explains that about ten tunes he improvised in the studio were credited to another name, and they told ASCAP the royalties belong to Slam.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Now, you were -- well, now, since we're talking about France, --
Now, you had, you and your wife Claire (PHONETIC) who's here with us, --
-- mentioned the fact that there was some other music that you did, that you came up with some tunes in the studio. And what did you say was happening, Claire?

Well, he -- I would say there are probably ten songs that he came up with in the studio that he named and are -- on the record, are given credit as Ogner Bozer (PHONETIC). Now, ASCAP has received a letter that they want to claim the royalties on it.
The producer of the record? The record

Yes, the record company, who is also the producer. It's the same person. And what we have done is to inform ASCAP that all of our rights are, you know, belong to us and informed ASCAP that he would collect his own royalties on his own songs and they're not to be assigned to anybody but Slam Stewart.
